claims.quote: 233 mm in Lake Michigan to 144 mm in Saginaw Bay

claims.claim: faster-growing perch stocks mature younger but at larger sizes
claims.location: p. 2059 (PDF p. 1), abstract; p. 2064 (PDF p. 6), Results
claims.quote: faster-growing stocks were mature at younger ages but larger sizes
claims.conditions: growth indexed by mean length at age 2; across 13 stocks; the female A50–growth relation was strongly driven by Lake Michigan and Georgian Bay, the L50–growth relation held without the influential stocks

claims.claim: maturity at females 11–18 cm, males 8–13 cm (Feiner et al. 2017)
claims.source_value: female L50 144–233 mm TL (most stocks 160–200 mm); male L50 128–190 mm TL (most 160–200 mm); female PMRN midpoints (Lp50,a) ~144–205 mm (Fig. 3a)
claims.quote: in Les Cheneaux to 128 mm in southern Lake Michigan
claims.note: 11–18 / 8–13 cm is not in Feiner et al.; it is below every Great Lakes stock (the smallest female L50 is 14.4 cm, the smallest male 12.8 cm). If the sim's sizes come from stunted northern perch (e.g. Munro & MacMillan 2012), cite that; Feiner et al. support only the direction (faster growth → younger, larger)

tried.note: accepted manuscript (TSpace), 45 pages; read first, then replaced by the published version — values identical; saved as docs/research_notes/fetched/v2/Feiner_etal_2017.accepted_manuscript.pdf

notes: Males reached 50 % maturity at younger ages than females in every stock, and within stocks males matured smaller. Male Lp50 rose with growth while female Lp50 fell (sex-specific trade-offs). The paper's use is right except the species.js comment, which credits Feiner et al. with sizes they do not give. The NOAA copy carries a 'downloaded ... For personal use only' stamp from the publisher; it is the agency repository's open copy.
